chunks: Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said:
'I wonder at the one who eats the like of this' – and he gestured with his hand – 'and does not drink water after it; how does his stomach not burst?'

key_terms.تَنْشَقُّ: To burst, split, or rupture; hyperbolic expression emphasizing the danger of not drinking
key_terms.عَجَباً: Expression of wonder or astonishment; used rhetorically to indicate disapproval or concern
key_terms.مَعِدَة: Stomach; in classical Arabic medicine, the seat of digestion

ai.seo_question: Is it recommended in Islam to drink water after eating?
ai.summary: Imam Abu al-Hasan (Ali al-Hadi, peace be upon him) expresses astonishment at anyone who eats a large meal without drinking water afterward, rhetorically questioning how their stomach does not rupture. This hadith reflects the Imam's practical health guidance rooted in the medical understanding of his era, in which water after food was considered essential for proper digestion. The narration was transmitted through Yasir al-Khadim, a close servant of the Imam, indicating this was personal advice given in an intimate domestic setting.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad, from one of his companions, from Yasser who said, 
‘Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> said:

‘I<sup>asws</sup> wonder at the one who eats the like of that’ – and he<sup>asws</sup> gestured by his<sup>asws</sup> hand (eats a lot) – ‘and he does not drink water over it, how come his stomach does not burst’.
en.sarwar: Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from certain persons of his people from Yasir who have said the following: “Abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, once said, ‘I wonder about the one who eats ‘this much,’ making a hand gesture, ‘and does not drink any water on it, how is it that his stomach does not burst.’”
